title_en: Zhang Chuanjie v. Shanghai Jinghao Labor Service Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over labor contract
ruling_gist_en: For workers engaged in operations exposed to occupational disease hazards who have not undergone pre-departure occupational health examinations, the employer shall not dissolve or terminate the labor contract concluded with them. full_text_en:
Zhang Chuanjie v. Shanghai Jinghao Labor Service Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over labor contract

Ruling Summary

Where a worker engaged in an operation exposed to occupational disease hazards has not undergone a pre-departure occupational health examination, the employer shall not rescind or terminate the labor contract concluded with such worker. Even if the employer and the worker have reached a mutual agreement to rescind the labor contract, the rescission agreement shall be deemed invalid.

Plaintiff: Zhang Chuanjie, male, 47 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Funan County, Anhui Province.

Defendant: Shanghai Jinghao Labor Service Co., Ltd., domiciled at Chuansha New Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Legal representative: Wang Wenqing, Manager of the Company.

Defendant: China Shipping Industry (Shanghai Changxing) Co., Ltd., domiciled at Changxing Island, Chongming County, Shanghai.

Legal representative: Zhang Yibing, Chairman of the Company.

The plaintiff, Zhang Chuanjie, filed an action with the Chongming County People's Court of Shanghai against the defendants, Shanghai Jinghao Labor Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinghao Company) and China Shipping Industry (Shanghai Changxing) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as China Shipping Company), concerning a dispute over a labor dispatch contract.

The plaintiff, Zhang Chuanjie, alleged: In October 2007, the plaintiff entered into a labor contract with Shanghai Xingxu Labor Service Co., Ltd., whose legal representative was Wang Wenqing. In January 2010, the plaintiff was transferred to the defendant Jinghao Company, also represented by Wang Wenqing as its legal representative. Since October 2007, the plaintiff had been dispatched to the defendant China Shipping Company to work as an electric welder. On January 13, 2014, Jinghao Company and the plaintiff signed an agreement for the mutual rescission of the labor contract. The plaintiff requested a pre-departure occupational health examination, and Jinghao Company promised to arrange the examination for the plaintiff after signing the agreement, but changed its mind the next day. Only after the plaintiff complained to the relevant authorities did Jinghao Company arrange the examination. The plaintiff argued that the agreement for mutual rescission of the labor contract signed with Jinghao Company was a standard form contract provided by Jinghao Company. Although the agreement stated that the plaintiff had proposed the rescission of the labor relationship, it was actually Jinghao Company that had proposed the rescission. The plaintiff filed for arbitration and litigation, requesting that the labor relationship between the plaintiff and Jinghao Company be reinstated as of January 13, 2014.

The defendants, Jinghao Company and China Shipping Company, argued: The plaintiff, Zhang Chuanjie, and Jinghao Company had already reached an agreement to rescind the labor relationship on January 13, 2014, and compensation had been paid. Since the plaintiff had already left the defendants for over a year, they disagreed with reinstating the labor relationship.

The Chongming County People's Court of Shanghai found at first instance:

In January 2010, the plaintiff, Zhang Chuanjie, established a labor relationship with the defendant Jinghao Company and was subsequently dispatched to the defendant China Shipping Company to work as an electric welder. The last labor contract signed between the parties was valid from January 1, 2010, to June 30, 2014. On January 13, 2014, Jinghao Company (Party A) and the plaintiff (Party B) signed an agreement for the mutual rescission of the labor contract. The agreement stated that Party A and Party B mutually agreed to rescind the labor relationship as of January 13, 2014, and that the rights and obligations under the labor contract would terminate; Party A would pay Party B a lump sum of RMB 48,160, which included economic compensation for the rescission of the labor contract, other earned labor remuneration, and welfare benefits. Jinghao Company paid RMB 48,160 to the plaintiff on January 21, 2014.

In April 2014, the plaintiff, Zhang Chuanjie, was diagnosed by Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital with Stage I welder's pneumoconiosis. On December 10, 2014, the plaintiff was assessed by the Shanghai Labor Ability Appraisal Committee as having a Grade VII disability due to occupational disease. On November 27, 2014, the plaintiff applied for arbitration to the Chongming County Labor Personnel Dispute Arbitration Committee of Shanghai, requesting that the labor relationship with Jinghao Company be reinstated as of January 13, 2014. The Committee ruled against the plaintiff's request.

The Chongming County People's Court of Shanghai held at first instance:

Where a worker engaged in an operation exposed to occupational disease hazards has not undergone a pre-departure occupational health examination, or where a worker suspected of having an occupational disease is undergoing diagnosis or medical observation, the employer shall not rescind the labor contract in accordance with Articles 40 and 41 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. In the present case, the plaintiff and the defendant mutually agreed to rescind the labor relationship, which does not fall under the circumstances specified in Articles 40 and 41 of the said Law, and the rescission was a genuine expression of the parties' intent. The plaintiff, Zhang Chuanjie, had a Grade VII disability due to occupational disease, and the parties' labor contract had also expired. Since the defendant Jinghao Company disagreed with reinstating the labor relationship, the plaintiff's request to reinstate the labor relationship with Jinghao Company as of January 13, 2014, lacked legal basis and was not supported.

Accordingly, the Chongming County People's Court of Shanghai, in accordance with Articles 36, 41, and 42 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a judgment on June 24, 2015:

The plaintiff's claim for reinstatement of the labor relationship with Shanghai Jinghao Labor Service Co., Ltd. as of January 13, 2014, was rejected.

Zhang Chuanjie, dissatisfied, appealed to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, arguing: Although Zhang Chuanjie and Jinghao Company signed the "Agreement for Mutual Rescission of Labor Contract" on January 13, 2014, due to Jinghao Company's fault, Zhang Chuanjie was not assessed as having a "Grade VII disability due to occupational disease" until December 2014. Jinghao Company failed to arrange a pre-departure occupational health examination for him, violating the relevant provisions of the Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases of the People's Republic of China, and therefore the labor contract could not be rescinded beforehand. Accordingly, he requested the court to order the reinstatement of the labor relationship between Zhang Chuanjie and Jinghao Company as of January 13, 2014.

The appellees, Jinghao Company and China Shipping Company, jointly argued: The parties had mutually agreed to rescind the labor contract. The appellant, Zhang Chuanjie, was assessed as having a "Grade VII disability due to occupational disease," and the rescission of the labor relationship did not violate the relevant provisions of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, they disagreed with reinstating the labor relationship with Zhang Chuanjie. In summary, they requested that Zhang Chuanjie's appeal be dismissed.

After the second instance, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The issue in dispute in this case was: Where a worker engaged in an operation exposed to occupational disease hazards has not undergone a pre-departure occupational health examination, is an agreement between the employer and the worker to mutually rescind the labor contract automatically valid?

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

In accordance with the first paragraph of Article 42 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, where a worker engaged in an operation exposed to occupational disease hazards has not undergone a pre-departure occupational health examination, the employer shall not rescind the labor contract in accordance with Articles 40 and 41 of the said Law. Although this provision does not expressly exclude the situation where the employer and the worker mutually agree to rescind the labor contract, according to Article 36 of the Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases of the People's Republic of China, "For workers engaged in operations exposed to occupational disease hazards, the employer shall, in accordance with the provisions of the safety production supervision and management department and the health administrative department of the State Council, organize pre-employment, in-service, and pre-departure occupational health examinations, and inform the workers of the examination results in writing... For workers who have not undergone a pre-departure occupational health examination, [the employer] shall not rescind or terminate the labor contract concluded with them." Therefore, it is the employer's legal obligation to arrange pre-departure occupational health examinations for workers engaged in operations exposed to occupational disease hazards, and this obligation is not automatically exempted simply because the worker and the employer have mutually agreed to rescind the labor contract.

In this case, the "Agreement for Mutual Rescission of Labor Contract" signed by the parties on January 13, 2014, did not expressly state that the appellant, Zhang Chuanjie, had known of and waived his right to undergo a pre-departure occupational health examination. Moreover, Zhang Chuanjie had actively sought, through various channels, to require the appellee Jinghao Company to arrange a pre-departure occupational health examination for him. Therefore, Zhang Chuanjie had not waived his right to assert such a claim, and Jinghao Company should have arranged the pre-departure occupational health examination for him. Before the conclusion of the assessment of Zhang Chuanjie's occupational disease, the labor relationship between the parties could not be automatically rescinded.

On December 10, 2014, the appellant, Zhang Chuanjie, was assessed as having a "Grade VII disability due to occupational disease." According to Article 37 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, where a worker is assessed as having a Grade 7 to 10 disability due to work-related injury, if the labor or employment contract expires and is terminated, or if the worker himself proposes to rescind the labor or employment contract, the work-related injury insurance fund shall pay a lump-sum medical subsidy for work-related injuries, and the employer shall pay a lump-sum employment subsidy for disability. Therefore, given that the labor contract originally signed by the parties was due to expire on June 30, 2014, and Zhang Chuanjie was assessed as having a "Grade VII disability due to occupational disease" on December 10, 2014, in accordance with the provisions of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, the employer could terminate the expired contract. Accordingly, the labor relationship between Zhang Chuanjie and the appellee Jinghao Company should be terminated as of December 10, 2014.

In conclusion, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 36 of the Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases of the People's Republic of China, Article 37 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, and Item (2) of the first paragraph of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a judgment on November 12, 2015:

1. The civil judgment (2015) Chong Min Yi (Min) Chu Zi No. 1021 of the Chongming County People's Court of Shanghai was set aside;

2. The labor relationship between the appellant, Zhang Chuanjie, and the appellee, Shanghai Jinghao Labor Service Co., Ltd., was reinstated as of January 13, 2014, and terminated on December 10, 2014.

This judgment is final.
